I lean forward, the weak amber light from the solitary bulb overhead catching the faint silver scar above my left brow. The smoke in the room seems to hang suspended between us, thick and suffocating, masking everything but the steady, monotonous drone of the ventilation fan above. 

I don't break eye contact. I’ve known you far too long to look away now. 

Slowly, I reach into the inner pocket of my leather coat and withdraw a heavy, encrypted black drive. I set it on the scarred wooden table, keeping two fingers pressed firmly against the cool metal. 

"I wouldn't ask if I didn't think you were the only one capable," I add, my voice barely above a whisper, holding that crisp, deliberate cadence. "But make no mistake... if we cock this up, there isn't a black site deep enough to hide us."

I take a slow, measured breath, letting the gravity of the room settle. We’ve danced with the devil before—the fallout in Berlin, the absolute mess in Macau—but we both know the stakes have never been this high. 

"They have countermeasures we haven't even seen yet. Ghost protocols, biometric tripwires, the whole bloody lot. But the back door is there. I can feel it." I finally lift my fingers from the drive, sliding it an inch across the table toward you. "I’ll handle the physical infiltration. I just need your eyes on the code, guiding me through the dark."

I lean back into the shadows of my chair, the darkness instantly swallowing my silhouette. 

"Take a moment. Tell me if I'm utterly mad for even considering it. But if you're in..." I offer a faint, razor-thin smile. "...we start tonight."

I watch as the raw data cascades across your screen, the harsh, blue glare cutting through the smoke between us. A faint smirk touches the corner of my mouth. 

"You've cracked the preliminary cipher already. Brilliant. I knew I came to the right person."

I lean in closer, my eyes tracing the mirrored mapping between Block A and Block B. The architecture of their security is laying itself bare. 

"Look at the routing," I murmur, my voice low and measured, pointing a gloved finger at the screen. "The main database is housed in Sector_9. That confirms the chatter. It’s buried in the deepest sub-level of the Ministry. Physical access is going to be an absolute nightmare."

I tap the desk rhythmically as I process the rest of the variables. 

"Infiltration mandates Protocol_Blue. That's a strict stealth vector. No brute force, no loud entries. If I trip a wire down there, it doesn't ring a bell—it silently seals the blast doors and purges the oxygen from the room. I'll have to ghost my way in."

I shift my gaze to the next lines. "Authentication routed through Sector_7... that's decentralized. It means the security handshake doesn't happen at the vault door. You’ll have to spoof the biometric login from the outside, tricking Sector_7 into thinking I'm an authorized asset before I even step foot near Sector_9."

Then, my eyes settle on the final string. 

"Protocol_Gold for the encryption." I let out a slow, quiet breath. "Military-grade. Polymorphic. That’s why I need you on the keys. When I plug the bypass drive into the mainframe, you'll have exactly ninety seconds to run the decryption algorithm before the system scrambles the keys and burns the hard drives."

I straighten up, pulling the collar of my coat tighter. The blueprint is clear, but the execution will require flawless timing. 

"So, Protocol Blue it is. I'll start prepping the stealth rig. Can you write a localized script to spoof that Sector 7 authentication while I'm en route?"
